rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the Prophet that the baseless dispute over God's signs should not worry him.
rows.anchor: This verse sounds an assurance to the Prophet (sws) that he should not wor ry about those who are baselessly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the preceding arguments for monotheism and the Hereafter, presented in various ways.
rows.anchor: The word “signs” refer to the arguments mentioned earlier which substantiate monotheism and the Hereafter in various styles.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents lack a counterargument; they resist because accepting the truth would acknowledge the Prophet's superiority and wound their leadership conceit.
rows.anchor: acknowledging his superiority over them. This of course would severely dent the conceit and vanity they have for their leadership.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance cannot succeed: God's verdict is to make truth prevail through the Prophet and humiliate his opponents in both worlds.
rows.anchor: He will make the truth dominant through the Prophet (sws) and these opponents of his will be humiliated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the arrogant may try to harm him, the Prophet should seek God's refuge; God sees and hears and will protect him from their evil.
rows.anchor: because of their arrogance, these people will try to harm him; but he should not worry and seek refuge with his God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrecting people is easier than creating the immense heavens and earth; failure to grasp this obvious argument is ignorance.
rows.anchor: How can it be difficult for the God Who can bring the heavens and the earth into existence to create mankind again?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the Hereafter, the world would leave everyone unaccountable and equate the blind with the perceptive and the wicked with the pious; this denies God's justice, wisdom, mercy, and power, so the Hereafter is certain.
rows.anchor: This obviously is not true. It negates the attributes of justice, wisdom, mercy and power of the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind are blind in intellect; those who see have visionary insight and reflect on God's signs.
rows.anchor: not only can see but also have visionary insight and are ones who reflect on the signs of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The facts are plain enough to understand; the failure lies in people's refusal to use their ears and eyes.
rows.anchor: these facts are not so concealed that no one is able to understand them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here arrogance also carries the sense of evasion.
rows.anchor: encompasses the meaning of evasion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling the Hereafter, the passage turns to monotheism and direct prayer to God.
rows.anchor: After reminding people of the Hereafter, a reminder is now sounded about monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requires no intermediary: anyone may ask Him directly, which rejects the idolaters' belief that access to God depends on deities as intercessors.
rows.anchor: no means or intermediary is required to ask from Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts every right supplication; when He delays or does not grant one, His wisdom makes the deferral good, so people should be content.
rows.anchor: the Almighty definitely accepts every right supplication. If He does not accept a supplication

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God has authority to accept or reject requests and knows the wisdom behind His actions; asking anyone else is useless.
rows.anchor: It is totally useless to go to someone other than God for requests because it is only He Who has the authority to accept or reject requests

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who arrogantly neglect worship despite God's open invitation will soon enter Hell in humiliation.
rows.anchor: those who are showing indifference in worshipping Him merely because of arrogance should remember that soon they will enter Hell in a humiliating way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses the same opponents described in verse 56: political ambition and fear of inferiority, not doubt or argument, drive their evasion and lead to humiliation.
rows.anchor: Earlier in verse 56 it has been stated that those who are opposing Muḥammad (sws) are not doing so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context indicates ellipsis: “dark” after “night” and the purpose clause after “bright” are suppressed.
rows.anchor: are suppressed because of contextual indications

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs establish the Hereafter through providence and monotheism through the harmony within creation.
rows.anchor: With respect to the providence found in them, they substantiate the Hereafter and with respect to the harmony found in them they substantiate monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made a dark, moderate night for rest and a lit day for work; these provisions are a great favor, though most people are ungrateful.
rows.anchor: He created the day to cater for their livelihood activities, He also created the night for them to provide them with peace and comfort.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day-night cycle displays God's mercy and power: people could not alter continuous day or night, and the design should lead them to gratitude.
rows.anchor: had He wanted only the day to exist continuously no one could have stopped Him
